Costs were calculated using the Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority’s (PREPA’s) time- of-use rate structure, which applies to customers with peak demand exceeding 1 MW, aligned with the modeled system performance (PREPA 2019): o Peak hours (9 a.m.–10 p.m.): $0.05779/kWh o Off-peak hours (10:00 PM – 9:00 AM): $0.01879/kWh The time-of-use rate structure significantly affected the cost profile, particularly for chiller operation, which aligns with peak daytime hours. The total annual electricity cost for the central cooling system, including chillers, cooling towers, and circulation pumps, was estimated at approximately $150,000, with chillers accounting for 75.3% of the total electricity consumption, primarily due to the mechanical cooling relative to the other components. • Water Costs: Water consumption during operation arises primarily from cooling tower evaporation losses and associated blowdown, a standard process in which a portion of water is intentionally discharged to remove dissolved solids that accumulate due to evaporation. This blowdown water is replaced with fresh makeup water to maintain system performance and prevent scaling, corrosion, and other operational issues. Hourly cooling tower flow rates (in GPM) were estimated by converting hourly thermal load rejection (in tons) using a conversion factor of 2.48 GPM per ton, estimated based on the system flow rate and cooling tower capacity (the information obtained from the site visit). An evaporation loss rate of 2% was applied, reflecting typical values and Puerto Rico’s climate conditions. Blowdown was estimated as an additional 0.5% of circulating flow, assuming a cycles-of-concentration value of 5, which represents standard practice for treated municipal water. The total water loss was used to calculate hourly makeup water volume. The water consumption was priced using a tiered pricing structure based on Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority rates: o Up to 100 m³: $2.68/m³ o 101–200 m³: $3.34/m³ o Above 200 m³: $4.38/m³. Hourly water volumes evaporated were multiplied by the applicable rate based on the consumption tier. The estimated annual water cost was approximately $241,193. 4.1.3 Levelized Cost of Cooling The estimated capital and operational costs were used to calculate the LCOC, a standardized metric for evaluating the long-term economic performance of a cooling system over its 27 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. operational lifetime.
